# m.partners.benzinga.news

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Benzinga news articles, with headline, teaser, body, and the tickers each one names.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.partners.benzinga.news(symbols=None, *, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

- [Query methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.APPEND`, which appends each row it hasn't seen, identified by `BenzingaId` and `Symbol`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows the [shared rules](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | US stock tickers; None, the default, for no ticker filter (`dm.ALL` is refused). |
| [`start`](README.md#start) | The earliest publication time; `poll()` needs it or a `limit`. |
| [`end`](README.md#end) | The end of the range. |
| [`sort`](README.md#sort) | Massive's field to sort by, such as `"published"`. Fields: any REST field under [Massive fields](#massive-fields). |
| [`order`](README.md#order) | The direction of `sort`. |
| [`limit`](README.md#limit) | The most rows to return, in total. |
| [`filters`](README.md#filters) | Such as `{"channels_any_of": ["earnings"]}`. Keys: `author`, `author_any_of`, `author_gt`, `author_gte`, `author_lt`, `author_lte`, `channels`, `channels_all_of`, `channels_any_of`, `stocks`, `stocks_all_of`, `stocks_any_of`, `tags`, `tags_all_of`, `tags_any_of`. |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Real-time Benzinga News (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Benzinga News | Updated in real time, All history |
| Benzinga News Business | Updated in real time, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The ticker the request named that the row lists in `Tickers`: a row that lists several of the named tickers appears once for each, so an article about AAPL and MSFT read for both is listed under each. A request that named one ticker gives it to every row. Null when the call named no ticker, and on a row that lists none of a request's named tickers. |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `published`: "The timestamp (formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp) when the news article was originally published." |
| `Author` | String | The name of the journalist or entity that authored the news article. |
| `BenzingaId` | long | The identifier used by Benzinga for this record. |
| `Body` | String | The full text content of the news article. |
| `Channels` | String[] | A list of categories or topics that the article belongs to (e.g., 'News', 'Price Target'). |
| `Images` | String[] | A list of images associated with the article. |
| `LastUpdated` | Instant | The timestamp (formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp) when the news article was last updated in the system. |
| `Tags` | String[] | A list of tags that describe the themes or content of the article. |
| `Teaser` | String | A short summary or lead-in to the news article's content. |
| `Tickers` | String[] | A list of stock or crypto tickers mentioned in the article. |
| `Title` | String | The headline of the news article. |
| `Url` | String | The direct link to the source of the news article. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. |
